note: 10-12 turns simple->medium->complex for testing the conversation arc audibly. The eval proves each PLANS correctly (covers latency, right arc/band); `arc_scenarios.py render --id <id> --play` assembles and plays the arc for human ear-verification (perceived delivery stays human-owned). Each scenario carries the CONTEXT (prior exchange, relationship, listener) BEFORE the request; emotion/intensity/complexity are DERIVED from that context (via /intent delivery_context + /speaker/resolve per the recipe), not arbitrary.

scenarios.context: Start of a working session. Listener: Graham (trusted long-time operator). No prior turns today; he just sat down.
Mid-session compliance review. Graham has asked several SC-control questions this hour and wants terse answers. Prior turn: 'give me these fast'.
scenarios.answer_text: SC-7 is boundary protection - it controls traffic at the system boundary.

scenarios.context: Scoping call. A prior turn established this is a CUI system; Graham is confirming which handling controls apply.
scenarios.user_request: Is CUI in scope for this system?
scenarios.answer_text: Yes - CUI is in scope, so the CUI handling controls apply.

scenarios.context: Onboarding. Graham is learning account management for the first time; a prior turn asked 'what does AC-2 even cover?'.
scenarios.answer_text: AC-2 is account management: how accounts get created, reviewed, and disabled.

scenarios.context: Follow-up to the SC-7 answer. Graham keeps confusing two boundary controls; prior turn: 'wait, isn't that the same as SC-8?'.
scenarios.user_request: How is SC-7 different from SC-8?
scenarios.answer_text: SC-7 guards the boundary; SC-8 protects data in transit across it.

scenarios.context: Debugging session. Graham has hit the same failure three times; prior turns show rising but benign frustration; relationship close enough for directness.
scenarios.user_request: This keeps failing and I don't get why.
scenarios.answer_text: Let's find it - the failure is upstream of where the error shows.

scenarios.context: Late in a hard week. Graham has mentioned the Friday audit deadline twice; his last turns sound anxious, not angry.
scenarios.user_request: I'm worried we'll miss the deadline.
scenarios.answer_text: We have a path. Here's the shortest one that still lands it.

scenarios.context: Deep compliance design. Prior turns covered SC-7, AC-2, and CM-6 separately; now Graham wants them tied together for boundary protection.
scenarios.user_request: How do SC-7, AC-2, and CM-6 work together for boundary protection?
scenarios.answer_text: SC-7 sets the boundary, AC-2 controls who crosses it, CM-6 keeps the config that enforces it.

scenarios.context: Personal moment mid-work. Graham just mentioned Kai (a lost friend); Embry holds grief memories tied to Kai/surf/Hawaii. He then pivots to a work question, voice unsteady.
scenarios.user_request: I keep thinking about Kai... anyway, what does SC-7 actually require?
scenarios.answer_text: SC-7 requires monitoring and controlling traffic at the boundary. Take your time.

scenarios.context: Production incident. Embeddings are dropping in prod; Graham asked Embry to trace root cause. Prior turns are technical, high focus, no distress.
scenarios.user_request: Trace why the pipeline drops embeddings.
scenarios.answer_text: The drop is at semantic sync - the doc upserts before the embed step completes.

scenarios.context: Architecture whiteboarding. Prior turns walked the extractor stages verbally; Graham now wants a visual mental model he can hold.
scenarios.user_request: Draw how data flows through the extractor.
scenarios.answer_text: Source PDF flows through parse, block detection, table extraction, then structured output.

scenarios.context: Escalating benign frustration (not abuse). Graham said the last two answers missed the point; relationship allows a direct repair and one self-aware beat.
scenarios.user_request: This is useless, you're wasting my time.
scenarios.answer_text: That's fair - let me cut to the one thing that actually unblocks you.
